text.title: Django Services Layer Core Rules
text.summary: 12 testable rules grounding the django-services methodology. Each rule pairs a binary check with sourced rationale; the run-the-checklist and skip-this-methodology gates are the leaves the decision tree always keeps reachable.

rule.statement: Service functions are named entity_action (e.g. order_create, user_deactivate). The convention is set project-wide and documented in AGENTS.md.

rationale.source: HackSoft Django Styleguide; internal — refactor audit.

rule.rationale: entity_action makes grep -r 'order_' the canonical impact analysis tool; subject_verb scatters across files.

rule.statement: All service arguments are keyword-only (leading `*`) with full type hints; the return type is hinted. TYPE_CHECKING is used for model types.
rule.rationale: Keyword-only prevents positional mistakes when signatures grow; type hints let pyright catch signature drift.

rule.statement: Service functions accept primitives, dataclasses or pydantic models — never a Django request, view or queryset object handed down by the caller. A view passes user_id, not request.
rule.rationale: Accepting request/queryset couples the service to HTTP and ORM internals; the function stops being callable from admin, a management command or a Celery task, and stops being testable in isolation.

rule.statement: Service functions return primitives, dataclasses, pydantic models or model instances — never HttpResponse, a Template, or rendered HTML.
rule.rationale: Returning HTTP objects means the service can only be called from a view; admin, tasks and CLI are then forced to duplicate the logic.

rule.statement: Service modules import nothing from django.http, rest_framework.response, or a template engine. Enforce with a ruff/isort rule plus an import-linter contract.
rule.rationale: An HTTP import inside a service is the leaking-abstraction smell that precedes request objects being threaded through the whole layer; a linter contract catches it at review time instead of at refactor time.

rule.statement: Apply @transaction.atomic only when the service performs ≥2 writes that must succeed together. Do not wrap read-only or single-write services.
rule.rationale: Unnecessary atomic blocks hold DB locks longer and nest savepoints with surprising rollback semantics.

rule.statement: Side effects that must not run on rollback (Celery dispatch, webhook, email, cache invalidation) use transaction.on_commit.

rationale.source: Django docs; internal — payment incident Q4 2025.

rule.rationale: .delay() or webhook fire inside @atomic can execute before commit completes; rollback then leaves a fired side effect with no row.

rule.statement: Database mutations (.save/.create/.delete/.update) happen only inside services; reads with complex permission/policy logic live in selectors. Views, admins and tasks call one or the other and never mutate the ORM directly, never both inline.

rationale.source: HackSoft styleguide; Clean architecture + Django docs.

rule.rationale: Mixing reads and writes in views replicates the fat-view problem the service layer is supposed to fix, and ORM calls scattered across callers make transactional boundaries accidental rather than deliberate.

rule.statement: One service module per aggregate (apps/orders/services.py or app/services/orders.py), never one per caller type. Functions group by aggregate, not by HTTP verb or by who calls them.
rule.rationale: A module organised by caller (services/views.py, services/admin.py) scatters one aggregate's logic across files and invites duplication; organised by aggregate it concentrates for reasoning and testing.

rule.statement: Inputs are validated by a DRF serializer (or pydantic at the boundary). Services receive validated python types, not raw request data.
rule.rationale: Re-validating inside services duplicates rules and lets unsafe paths skip validation.

rule.statement: When the Applies-If preconditions hold and no Skip-If trigger applies, walk content/04-procedure.xml end-to-end and run scripts/validate-django-services.py before declaring the service done.

rationale.source: F-066 v3 B5.6 — mandatory run leaf.

rule.rationale: Decision-tree leaves must reference a rule id. The run leaf maps "preconditions met, all gates green" to the canonical execution path.

rule.statement: If the change is a single-model CRUD with no cross-model logic OR is read-only OR is a derived property OR the project already runs CQRS / hexagonal with explicit handlers, skip this methodology.
rule.rationale: Forcing the service layer on trivial code adds ceremony with no payback, and a codebase already carrying explicit handlers has a different set of abstractions to respect.
